standard.title: First Nations music and ICIP rights
standard.description: investigate the diversity of music composed and/or performed by First Nations Australians, considering culturally responsive approaches to Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore ways First Nations Australians use music to continue and revitalise culture (AC9AMU6E02). They have explored rather than investigated — they have not yet engaged with the specific question of Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property (ICIP) rights or considered the ethical responsibilities of listeners, performers and composers when engaging with First Nations music.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the diversity of music composed and/or performed by First Nations Australians and engage with culturally responsive approaches to Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights as they are relevant to their practice as listeners, composers and performers.

nodes.label: Diversity of First Nations Australian music
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the diversity of music composed and/or performed by First Nations Australians, including the range of styles, genres and cultural contexts represented
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate at least one First Nations Australian composer or performer; describe the styles or genres they draw on and how they communicate ideas or messages
nodes.typical_width: Investigate multiple First Nations Australian composers and/or performers across different styles and contexts; describe how each communicates ideas across communities and cultures
wider: Investigate the impacts of a First Nations Australian musician's or musicians' work — consider what communities or audiences they reach, how their music has been received, and what ideas or messages travel across cultural contexts
Explore how First Nations Australian musicians draw on multiple styles or genres in creating their own music — identify both traditional and contemporary musical influences in their work

response_modes.reason: Students need to encounter genuine diversity in First Nations Australian music before they can understand what 'diversity' means in this context. A narrow sample produces stereotyped understandings — breadth of artists, styles, regions and purposes builds the knowledge base for respectful, informed engagement.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The impact and cross-community communication direction is genuinely rich — investigating how First Nations musicians communicate ideas across cultures involves analysis of audience, reception and purpose that extends well beyond biographical or stylistic description.
success_criteria: Describes the work of at least one First Nations Australian composer or performer
Identifies at least one style or genre the musician draws on and how they use it to communicate

nodes.label: Understanding ICIP rights
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights are and why they exist, including when and how they might be relevant to music
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what ICIP rights are and give at least one example of when they might be relevant to music — as a listener, songwriter, composer or performer
nodes.typical_width: Explain why ICIP rights exist and how copyright and ICIP rights interact; identify scenarios relevant to music where ICIP rights are relevant and explain what they require
wider: Investigate a case study that illustrates protocols relating to ICIP rights in music — consider how the case clarifies when permission is required and what respectful engagement looks like

Investigate issues relating to the use of First Nations Australian languages or stories in lyrics, songs or screen-based music — identify the ethical questions these raise and the protocols that apply

response_modes.reason: Students often understand ICIP rights in the abstract but don't know how to apply them in practice. Encountering multiple specific contexts — listening, sampling, songwriting, performing — where the rights question arises helps students move from abstract understanding to practical ethical reasoning.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The case study direction provides genuinely rich analytical territory — examining a real case where ICIP rights were navigated (or violated) makes the ethical principles concrete and consequential in ways that abstract explanation cannot achieve.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one context in which ICIP rights are relevant to music practice

nodes.label: Applying culturally responsive approaches
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make ethical choices about how they engage with First Nations Australian music, using protocols for ICIP rights as a guide
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least one protocol question to their own practice (e.g. 'Who wrote this music?', 'May I use ideas from this, and do I need permission?'); explain the reasoning behind the protocol
nodes.typical_width: Apply multiple protocol questions to their own practice as listeners, composers and/or performers; explain how the protocols guide ethical engagement with First Nations Australian music
wider: Evaluate a scenario in which a creator used First Nations Australian music without following ICIP protocols — analyse the ethical issues raised and consider what the creator should have done differently

Develop a set of personal guidelines for culturally responsive engagement with First Nations Australian music — based on the protocols investigated, articulate what they will do as a listener, composer and performer

response_modes.reason: Applying protocols requires students to reason through specific situations — the ethical logic doesn't transfer automatically from principle to practice. Scaffolding the reasoning (who created this → what rights apply → what does that mean for what I want to do) makes the protocol application purposeful rather than checklist-driven.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The personal guidelines direction is genuinely rich — synthesising protocol knowledge into a personally owned set of principles reflects a deeper level of ethical reasoning than applying a given protocol to a given case.
success_criteria: Applies at least one protocol question to a real or hypothetical music practice scenario
Explains the ethical reasoning behind the protocol
